title: Ten Minutes by Tractor, Terroir Masterclass
summary: One hour in TMBT's private tasting room. Eight wines (two limited-release, six current), the three single-vineyard sites side-by-side, and the long answer to why Pinot from Main Ridge tastes the way it does.
venueName: Ten Minutes by Tractor Cellar Door
recurrenceNote: Available on request (check availability on TMBT website)
suitableFor: Adults 18+; wine enthusiasts; couples; small groups
accessibilityNotes: Cellar door fully accessible (wheelchair; stroller; transport accessible)
nearbyAttractions: Montalto; Paringa Estate; Merricks General Wine Store
suggestedItineraryPairing: Combine with lunch at TMBT Restaurant or Allis Wine Bar; add Merricks General Store for afternoon
editorVerdict: This is the masterclass for people who want to understand Pinot, not just drink it. The most serious 60 minutes of wine education on the Peninsula.
editorNote:
TMBT's three vineyards (McCutcheon, Wallis, Judd) sit minutes apart on Main Ridge and make wildly different Pinot and Chardonnay. The masterclass puts those wines next to each other on the bench, with a winemaker walking you through what changes between rows of vines a kilometre apart. Eight wines: two limited release, six current. Snacks on the table. Minimum two guests, private group only, $120 a head.

Built for people already a bit into wine. Not the entry-level tasting, this is the next step. Book directly through TMBT; the Tripadvisor listing has been on and off but the masterclass runs.

Do the masterclass mid-morning, then stay for lunch at TMBT Restaurant or walk down to Allis Wine Bar. Add Merricks General Store on the way home.
